- key_parameters: addH=TRUE/FALSE ;; Controls whether hydrogens are added/included when computing molecular weight (MW), molecular formula (MF), and atom counts. ;; type=1|2|3 ;; In cmp.search, controls the output format (1 for index, 2 for named vector of scores, 3 for data frame). ;; cutoff=value ;; Sets the similarity threshold for searches (cmp.search, fpSim) and clustering (cmp.cluster). ;; mode="a1a2b"|"a1b"|"b" ;; In jarvisPatrick, controls the strictness of the clustering requirements (strictness and runtime decrease from "b" to "a1a2b"). ;; extendedAttributes=TRUE ;; In read.SDFset, enables reading extended attributes of V3000 format SDFs. ;; updateByName=TRUE ;; In loadSdf/loadSmiles, overwrites existing database compounds with the same name.
- alternatives: ChemmineOB=An add-on package integrating OpenBabel for fast format conversions, 3D coordinate generation, and canonicalization. ;; fmcsR=An add-on package for Maximum Common Substructure (MCS) searching and clustering. ;; SQLite database=An alternative to sdfStream for storing and querying large compound datasets efficiently.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to import small molecule libraries, calculate chemical descriptors, perform virtual screening via similarity searches, cluster compounds by structural similarity, or visualize chemical structures.
- pitfalls: Missing hydrogens in input SD files can lead to incorrect molecular weight and formula calculations unless addH=TRUE is specified. ;; Importing V3000 format SDFs with extendedAttributes=TRUE produces ExtSDF objects, which may not be compatible with all standard SDF methods. ;; Jarvis-Patrick clustering with mode="b" has nearly quadratic run time and is not suitable for very large datasets. ;; write.SDFsplit can output a very large number of files, so it should always be run in a dedicated directory.

workflows.name: chemical_structure_analysis_and_clustering
workflows.intent: Import small molecules, calculate physicochemical properties, generate descriptors, perform similarity searches, cluster the compounds, and visualize the results.
input: sdfsample.sdf (SD file containing small molecule structures)
workflows.stages: 1. Import and validate SDF structures ;; 2. Calculate molecular weight, formula, and atom counts ;; 3. Generate atom pair descriptors ;; 4. Perform structural similarity search ;; 5. Cluster compounds using binning clustering ;; 6. Plot chemical structures
workflows.code:
sdfset <- read.SDFset("http://faculty.ucr.edu/~tgirke/Documents/R_BioCond/Samples/sdfsample.sdf")
valid <- validSDF(sdfset)
sdfset <- sdfset[valid]
propma <- data.frame(MF=MF(sdfset), MW=MW(sdfset), atomcountMA(sdfset))
apset <- sdf2ap(sdfset)
cmp.search(apset, apset[1], type=3, cutoff = 0.3, quiet=TRUE)
clusters <- cmp.cluster(db=apset, cutoff = c(0.7, 0.8, 0.9), quiet = TRUE)
plot(sdfset[1:4], regenCoords=TRUE,print=FALSE)

workflows.name: database_storage_and_querying
workflows.intent: Store small molecules in an SQLite database, extract custom features, and perform fast SQL-like queries to retrieve compounds.
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize SQLite database ;; 2. Load compounds and extract custom features (e.g., ring counts) ;; 3. Query compounds based on feature criteria ;; 4. Retrieve matching compounds as an SDFset
workflows.code:
conn <- initDb("test.db")
ids<-loadSdf(conn,sdfsample, function(sdfset) data.frame(rings(sdfset,type="count",upper=6, arom=TRUE)) )
results = findCompounds(conn,"rings",c("rings <= 1"))
compounds = getCompounds(conn,results)

workflows.name: large_sdf_streaming
workflows.intent: Stream through a massive SD file to compute descriptors and index molecule positions without loading the entire file into memory.
input: test.sdf (Large SD file containing small molecules)
workflows.stages: 1. Define a descriptor extraction function ;; 2. Stream through the SDF and write descriptors to a tabular file ;; 3. Filter the tabular index and retrieve specific molecules of interest
workflows.code:
desc <- function(sdfset) cbind(SDFID=sdfid(sdfset), MW=MW(sdfset), groups(sdfset), APFP=desc2fp(x=sdf2ap(sdfset), descnames=1024, type="character"), AP=sdf2ap(sdfset, type="character"), rings(sdfset, type="count", upper=6, arom=TRUE) )
sdfStream(input="test.sdf", output="matrix.xls", fct=desc, Nlines=1000)
indexDF <- read.delim("matrix.xls", row.names=1)[,1:4]
indexDFsub <- indexDF[indexDF$MW < 400, ]
sdfset <- read.SDFindex(file="test.sdf", index=indexDFsub, type="SDFset")
